_comment: Level 100 parity measurement boxes, 640x480. THESE ARE DETECTORS, NOT DIAGNOSES. A box mean cannot distinguish 'the same object rendered wrong' from 'a different object occupying those pixels', and on this project that confusion has produced four false diagnoses. Before attributing any box's error to shading, split it by what each image is actually drawing there. See _caveats below for boxes with measured contamination, and tools/cockpit_intersection_mask_probe.py for the geometric-mask technique that replaces a box mean.

_caveats.cockpit frame (left): 19-27% NON-COCKPIT. Measured 2026-07-26 by counting the winning part at every pixel of a retail-pose z-buffered raster: this box is Object03 (6,739 px) plus Lsidebit01 (400 px). On the same-surface mask the shading is close; the box mean is dominated by silhouette disagreement, not by shading. Do not read this box as a cockpit shading metric.
_caveats.cockpit frame (right): 19% NON-COCKPIT. The box is Object01 (6,125 px) and nothing else, and Object01's shading is correct to 1.5% (retail/build 0.992/0.985/0.985 over 5,566 same-surface px). 1,713 of the box's 9,000 px are bright scene in retail and cockpit in the build, because our Object01 covers 8,856 px against retail's 6,306. R-channel decomposition is exact: +15.89 (build-only) +7.06 (both) +0.99 (neither) -1.86 (retail-only) = +22.08 against a measured 22.1 gap. That deficit is the 2.8774 degree composition residual, and it is the floor on this box. Do not read this box as a cockpit shading metric.
_caveats._note: Neither cockpit box contains Lsidebit02, which sits at y=371..420 below both.
_caveats.terrain mid-band: 38.86% CONTAMINATED by 'threat circle'. The two boxes intersect at [230,230,420,320] = 17,100 px of this box's 44,000. Measured 2026-07-26: that 38.9% of the area carries 66% of the box's material pixels (6,511 of 9,836). PROVEN CAUSALLY: commit dba2948e changed ONLY the compass gauge blend, yet moved this box 22.35 -> 20.75; with the threat box excised the real terrain moved 12.36 -> 12.27, i.e. 94% of that 'terrain' win was the compass overlay. Do NOT read this box as a terrain shading metric - use 'terrain mid-band (clean)'. Every historical number for this box, including the 91.15 -> 72.85 -> 65.12 sequence, is a blend of terrain and whatever the compass was doing.
_caveats.terrain mid-band (clean): 'terrain mid-band' minus the 'threat circle' intersection: 26,900 px, no HUD element. This is the box to use for terrain shading work. HAND-MEASURED at HEAD against retail t025065: 12.36% material / meanD 4.91, mean delta (ours-retail) [-0.77, +0.03, +0.81]. Split at x=320 the G channel FLIPS SIGN - left [-0.27, +0.53, +0.88], right [-1.30, -0.50, +0.73] - at magnitudes under 1.3 DN. That refutes a global-constant shading model rather than proving there is no residual: 12.36% material remains in pixels the threat circle never touches, and it is high-frequency, not an offset.
_caveats.scanner (lower left): PHASE-SENSITIVE at t025065, and that is what moved it 45.88 -> 47.97 across 2026-07-27. The tutorial's HUD emphasis brightens RadarOutline over rect (17,368,128x128), which lies ENTIRELY inside this box, so the box reads the emphasis SCHEDULE as if it were scanner shading. Measured 2026-07-27 (task #135) by dumping Core state per engine frame at ce2f6866 and at ad61cb1a under the capture's own input: player pose is BIT-IDENTICAL at the capture tick (yaw 509830 microrad, position 0,0, elevation 2111 mm on both) and the ONLY Core difference is Level100HudEmphasisMask - 0 at ce2f6866, 16 (Radar) at HEAD, because 016ebf38's message-box gate moved the radar emphasis window from ticks 379..561 to 567..755 and tick 752 is 3 ticks from its end. Retail's t025065 is NOT emphasised: our own un-emphasised frames score 45.94-46.08 against it where the emphasised ones score 47.97-52.33. So a change of ~2 points here is the documented ~0.69 s capture-epoch offset showing up, not a scanner defect. Score scanner work on a frame well inside or well outside the emphasis window, or state which state the frame is in.
_caveats._noise floors: RETAIL'S CROSS-RUN FLOOR IS NOT ONE NUMBER. The widely-quoted 0.02% is real and reproducible, but ONLY for full-frame at level-100 t025065 (verified: pristine-verification-2026-07-26/chain-20260726-164610 vs -164822 = 0.02% material, portrait/compass 0.00%). It does NOT generalise. Measured floors: frontend pages 1.28-5.57% (select-configuration worst); settled-camera level-100 full frame ~0.93%; speaker-portrait frames give portrait/compass 15.6-21.5% because retail's portrait carries a per-run non-deterministic dither. Opening-pan frames labelled 'reference-only (camera in motion)' reach 36.79% and must never be quoted as a floor. ALSO: our own capture self-noise at t025065 is ~2.53% full-frame, so any full-frame improvement under ~2.5 points is not measurable from a single capture pair.
